offence_severity: Sections 376, 302 and 201 of IPC: Minimum 7 years, Maximum 10 years (Section 302) and life imprisonment or death (Section 376)
number_of_offences: Charged with 3 offences, 3 offences finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The school leaving certificate was accepted as it was proved by examining the Head Mistress of the school, who recognized the signature of the Principal who issued it, and the evidence was not challenged.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the Head Mistress's evidence as credible since her testimony was not challenged and she recognized the signature of the Principal who issued the school leaving certificate.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant surrendered before the court on 13.06.2008.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 12/13-04-2008; Trial judgment: 30.05.2009; High Court decision: 29.10.2010; Supreme Court decision: 18.09.2013
legal_representation: Shankar Narayanan (for Gaurav Agrawal) for the Appellant; Jayesh Gaurav (for Gopal Prasad), Barun Kr. Sinha, Pratibha Sinha, Aayush Raj (for Rameshwar Prasad Goyal) for the Respondents
investigation_status: Charge sheet filed; application for age determination submitted; medical board opinion sought and accepted; case referred to Sessions Court; appeal filed and decided by High Court; appeal filed and decided by Supreme Court
appeal_history: Trial court: Case registered as Case No.132 of 2009; High Court: Criminal Revision No.504 of 2009 allowed, order of Sessions Judge set aside; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, order of Sessions Judge restored
prosecution_argument: The State argued that the school leaving certificate was false and fabricated, and that the medical board's opinion indicating the accused was about 20 years old on the date of occurrence should be accepted.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the school leaving certificate was properly proved through the head mistress of the school, and there was no cogent reason to discard it. They also submitted that the medical board's report should only be considered if the school leaving certificate was discarded.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that if the school leaving certificate is properly proved, there is no need for a medical examination by a medical board, as laid down in Ashwani Kumar Saxena v. State of M.P.
precedent_relied_upon: Ashwani Kumar Saxena v. State of M.P. 2012 (10) SCR 540
